answers.answer: 1. Start with 25 money. 2. Start with 1 active association worker on the notepad and 3 inactive workers lying on the spaces below it. 3. Draw 8 Zoo cards, keep 4 and discard 4 face up. 4. Draw 2 Final Scoring cards. 5. Put Animals side I in slot 1 (leftmost); put the other four Action cards randomly in slots 2–5, all side I up. 6. Appeal starts at 0 for the first player, 1 for second, 2 for third and 3 for fourth.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C1–F: 25 money; one active and three lying workers; draw 8, keep 4; draw 2 scoring cards; side I cards, Animals in leftmost slot; appeal staggered by turn order.

answers.answer: 1. At setup, reveal 4 face-up Base Conservation Projects below the Association board in a four-player game, and 3 in two- or three-player games. 2. In a two-player game only, block the left level on the left face-up project, the middle level on the middle project, and the right level on the right project; also block the three donation spaces in the donation area's left column. These are unavailable to both players. No such setup blocks are stated for three or four players. 3. Reveal the six-card display only after every player has selected starting hand cards.
answers.evidence: Setup 5b–5c: four cards in a 4-player game, otherwise three; 2-player blocked levels and donation column. Personal setup G reveals display after hands are chosen.

answers.answer: 1. After using the slot-4 card, remove it, shift the cards that were left of its now-empty slot one place right, and put the used card in slot 1. 2. Set strength before the action; each X-token spent then adds +1 strength and is returned to supply, but X-tokens gained during the action cannot boost that same action. 3. You may spend any number, but may hold at most 5 X-tokens. 4. Resolve an after-finishing effect only after the action is complete, including the Action-card movement.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: remove used card, shift cards left of empty slot right, place used card in slot 1; strength set before action; max 5 X-tokens; after-finishing after card movement.

answers.answer: 1. You may not take a regular action that plays zero animals or builds zero buildings; you cannot do nothing. 2. Instead you may choose the X-token alternative: select an Action card, move it to slot 1 using the ordinary card movement, and take exactly 1 X-token. 3. Its slot strength and upgrade side do not matter, and you cannot take it if you already hold 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and X-token action: zero animals/buildings is illegal; choose a card, move it to slot 1, gain 1 X-token; impossible at 5 held.

answers.answer: 1. If movement would go beyond the Break track's last space, ignore the excess steps. 2. The player who reaches the last space gains 1 X-token. 3. Finish the current turn; the break occurs afterward. 4. The summary specifies ordinary play resumes clockwise after the break with the next player; a break by itself does not add final turns (the separate game-end trigger during a break gives all players one more turn).
answers.evidence: Break track: last space triggers break after current turn, grants 1 X-token, ignores additional steps; break procedure continues clockwise. End-trigger clarification distinguishes break ending turns.

answers.answer: 1. Cards I advances the Break token 2 spaces, then either draws from the deck according to the strength table or snaps exactly 1 display card at strength 5+. Cards II also advances it 2 spaces, then draws from the deck and/or in-range display in any order under its table. 2. Cards I draw/discard at strengths 1–5 are 1/1, 1/0, 2/1, 2/0, 3/1; Cards II are 1/0, 2/1, 2/0, 3/1, 4/1. 3. Cards II snapping starts at strength 3 and takes exactly one display card; snap ignores reputation on either side and involves no deck draw. Reputation restriction applies only to the Cards II draw option. 4. Display cards taken during the turn are replenished after the turn ends. 5. There is no in-turn hand limit; discard to the limit only at breaks.
answers.evidence: Cards action: both sides advance Break 2; side I/II choices and snap rules; Cards draw tables; ordinary display refill at turn end; hand limit checked at breaks.

answers.answer: 1. Reputation range includes the display folder matching your reputation space and all lower-numbered folders. 2. Reputation 10 and above requires the upgraded Cards action (Cards II). 3. At space 15, further reputation leaves the counter at 15 and gives 1 appeal for each remaining reputation step. 4. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: Reputation track and display: range is matching folder plus lower folders; 10+ requires upgraded Cards; at 15 further rep converts to 1 appeal per step; no discard-pile inspection.

answers.answer: 1. Build I constructs exactly 1 building, of size no greater than strength; Build II constructs any number of different buildings whose total size is no greater than strength, but not two identical buildings in the same action. 2. Pay 2 money per space for each building before placing it. 3. The first building must have at least one space on a map border; later buildings must share at least one edge with an existing building. 4. Build only on empty spaces; do not overlap, go off-map, or cover water/rock. Restricted-icon spaces require Build II. 5. A kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from each other kiosk (at least 2 spaces between kiosks). 6. Each pavilion gives +1 appeal immediately, once.
answers.evidence: Build action table and placement rules: one vs many different, 2 money/space, first border/later adjacency, restrictions and kiosk spacing; pavilion appeal.

answers.answer: 1. Build I allows standard enclosures, kiosks, pavilions and one Petting Zoo; Build II additionally allows a Reptile House and a Large Bird Aviary. Each of the three special enclosure types is limited to one per individual zoo; the physical supply has four of each. 2. Unique buildings cannot be built through Build; they enter only through their Sponsor cards. 3. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately grants 7 appeal, and this may be triggered by any effect that covers the spaces.
answers.evidence: Buildings available through Build table; special-enclosure supply and zoo limit; Build II and unique buildings; full map rule.

answers.answer: 1. Yes. Benefits gained earlier during an action—including money, cards and newly activated workers—can be used in later steps of that same action; resolve items one at a time. 2. Pay for each item before receiving that item's own benefit. 3. Ordinary effects resolve immediately, while effects marked after finishing wait until the entire action and Action-card movement are complete. 4. When effects are simultaneous, the player whose effects they are chooses their order.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: earlier bonuses usable later in action; pay each item before benefits; after-finishing timing. Special Rules: owner chooses simultaneous-effect order.

answers.answer: 1. To play an Animal, meet every printed condition and pay its full cost first. A partner zoo from the animal's continent reduces cost by 3 money for each continent icon on that Animal card. 2. House ordinary animals in an empty standard enclosure at least the required size, then flip the entire enclosure to occupied; Petting Zoo animals go only in the Petting Zoo. Eligible reptiles and some birds may instead use their designated special enclosure, with enough marked capacity. 3. Special enclosures are never flipped: mark occupied spaces using one supply player token per required space; a Petting Zoo has 3 spaces and Reptile House/Aviary each have 5. 4. Meet any required distinct adjacent water or rock hexes; repeated edges touching the same terrain hex count once. These conditions also apply when using a special enclosure. 5. Resolve each animal's play effects: appeal and printed conservation/reputation; immediate effects before the next Animal, after-finishing effects after the whole Animals action and card movement. Simultaneous effects may be ordered by the player.
answers.evidence: Animals action: conditions, cost reduction, housing and terrain; special enclosure occupancy/capacities; effect timing and order.

answers.answer: 1. Animals II permits animals from hand or from the display within reputation range; display animals cost the folder number as an additional cost. 2. At strength 5+, you may gain 1 reputation at the very beginning of the action, before choosing/playing animals, so the new range applies. 3. Do not replenish display cards until the turn ends. 4. Animals II permits animals with the upgrade-required condition icon.
answers.evidence: Animals II: display play, folder-number cost, optional +1 reputation first at 5+, end-of-turn refill, upgrade-required animals.

answers.answer: 1. Only immediately when building a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary may you move suitable existing animals, moving all corresponding animals that fit and deciding separately for each. The new special enclosure must meet each animal's terrain requirements and have enough capacity. 2. Mark capacity with the animal's indicated number of player tokens from supply. 3. To free space for each moved animal, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all its requirements, including terrain; if none, flip the smallest occupied enclosure meeting its size alone; if none meets even its size requirement, flip none. 4. This relocation is distinct from release and is only available at construction, including construction through a permitted bonus.
answers.evidence: Moving existing animals into a newly built special enclosure: timing, all suitable animals, capacity, and standard-enclosure fallback.

answers.answer: 1. Association tasks have strengths 2 for +2 reputation, 3 for a partner zoo, 4 for a university, and 5 for conservation project work. 2. Association I performs exactly one task; Association II may perform one or more different tasks with total task value at most action strength, and may add at most one donation. 3. Each task requires at least one active worker. If one of your workers is already on that task, spend 2 workers to repeat it; with 3 of yours there, you cannot repeat until after a break. 4. Other players' workers do not affect whether you may use a task.
answers.evidence: Association action: task strengths, side I/II task limits, worker repetition rule, and other players' workers do not matter.

answers.answer: 1. Take partner zoos and universities from available spaces on the Association board and place them on the lowest empty spaces in the corresponding column of your zoo map; resolve any printed covered-space bonus immediately. Universities also immediately grant their own printed reputation award. 2. You cannot take duplicate universities; partner zoos must be from different continents. You may have at most 4 partner zoos; the third and fourth require Association II. 3. Board tiles are restocked at breaks (one of each continent/kind unless already owned by every player; no duplicate available tiles). A bonus granting one also uses an available Association-board tile. 4. The hand-limit university raises the break hand limit from 3 to 5; other universities do not change it.
answers.evidence: Association tasks; University tiles; break restock; FAQ bonus rules; map university hand-limit table.

answers.answer: 1. A Conservation Project can be played from hand with Association I/II conservation work, or from the display within reputation range with Association II and folder-number additional cost. A new project is placed above the board at the left, pushing others right. 2. To support, meet an unoccupied condition/level and place one of your seven left-edge map tokens on it; each reward level can hold only one token across all players, and you normally support a given project only once. 3. Gain its conservation and any shown reputation; remove the token from the map and take its map bonus immediately, before or after project reward as chosen. Recurring map bonuses repeat at each break. 4. A project pushed beyond the player-count limit is discarded; tokens on it return to their owners' supplies, while their map bonuses remain activated. Setup base projects below the board never move or replenish.
answers.evidence: Association conservation work: card entry, support and token rules, rewards/bonus timing, overflow and base-project distinction.

answers.answer: 1. The printed standard-enclosure requirement must fit the depicted release size category: 2− accepts size 1 or 2, 3 accepts size 3, and 4+ accepts size 4 or 5; it need not match one exact number within the 2−/4+ categories. 2. On release, lose only the animal's printed appeal before conservation reward; discard the animal and lose its icons. Keep its conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and previously earned effects. Playing a new release project gives 1 reputation; supporting a release project already in play does not. 3. If the animal could live in a special enclosure and its marked spaces can be removed, remove those tokens; otherwise free its standard enclosure by flipping the smallest occupied one meeting all requirements, or fallback to smallest meeting size alone, or none if none meets size. Flock animals follow this procedure too.
answers.evidence: Release into the wild: printed size categories, losses retained, new-project reputation, and enclosure freeing procedure.

answers.answer: 1. Sponsors I plays exactly one Sponsor from hand, requiring action strength at least its level and fulfillment of its conditions. Alternatively, advance Break by strength and take that much money. 2. Sponsors II may play one or more cards from hand and/or in-range display, paying each display card's folder number; strength +1 must be at least the sum of levels, and X-tokens can raise strength. Meet each card's conditions and fully resolve each card before the next, except after-finishing effects. 3. The Sponsors II break option pays double money, including if fewer steps remain than the chosen advance; the full money is still taken.
answers.evidence: Sponsors action: side I/II card counts, level budgets, display costs, sequence, and Break-for-money options.

answers.answer: 1. Break order: discard to hand limit; clear Multiplier/Venom/Constriction tokens; recall workers and restock Association tiles; discard display folders 1–2, compact and refill; take income; reset Break token. 2. Hand limit is normally 3, or 5 with the hand-limit university. 3. Each kiosk earns 1 money per adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, or pavilion. Empty standard enclosures do not count; empty special enclosures do. 4. If multiple players take display cards during break income, resolve clockwise from the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise from them), and refill after each such player's income before the next affected player chooses.
answers.evidence: Break procedure steps 1–6 and kiosk income; explicit break display-card ordering/refill rule.

answers.answer: 1. At 2 conservation, choose an Action-card upgrade or activate an additional association worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or an adjacent Bonus tile, if available. At 10, the first player to reach/pass it makes all players discard one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile. 2. Check game end at the end of your turn or during a break when Appeal and Conservation are in the same scoring area or have passed one another. Appeal gained during another player's turn waits until the end of your turn or a break, unless another trigger occurs first. 3. If triggered at your turn end, finish it and every other player takes one more turn; if during a break, all players take one more turn. 4. Each Final Scoring card is capped at 4 conservation points. VP = your Appeal minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area of your Conservation counter. Highest positive VP wins; ties go to most supported projects, then shared victory.
answers.evidence: Conservation milestones, end trigger and timing, final-turn rule, Final scoring cap and VP/tiebreak.

answers.answer: 1. Shuffle 9 Bonus tiles and place one at random face up on each of the four blank yellow spaces beside the Conservation track: two beside 5 and two beside 8. Do not use the two yellow spaces with icons; return the other five tiles to the box. 2. Physical component stock does not prohibit an otherwise legal play: use a suitable substitute if a component runs out. Explicit per-zoo limits and Association-board availability still apply.
answers.evidence: Global setup bonus tiles; Component supply: use suitable substitute, physical stock does not forbid legal play, explicit limits remain.

answers.answer: 1. Advanced maps 1–8 are selected by either taking two random maps and choosing one advanced side, or laying out player count +1 advanced maps and choosing in reverse play order; return unselected maps. 2. Map A starts with an empty size-3 standard enclosure and a kiosk on the indicated spaces; its printed kiosk counts as built, with a kiosk tile placed as a reminder.
answers.evidence: Personal setup A: advanced map selection methods; Map A ability and starting pieces.

answers.answer: 1. The seven conservation-support player tokens begin on the designated spaces along the left edge of each player's zoo map; remaining tokens stay beside the map. 2. When hiring inactive association workers, take them from the lowest supply space upward. 3. Some maps reward hiring the last worker with conservation points; the particular reward varies by printed map, and Map A's stated reward for the third partner zoo, not worker hiring, is a worker.
answers.evidence: Setup C2 and Map A bonuses; Special Rules says hire workers lowest reserve upward and certain maps give conservation for last worker.

answers.answer: 1. Flip a chosen Action card from side I to II in its current slot; it does not move. 2. Its side-II action becomes usable on your next action, while it counts as upgraded immediately for conditions. The current action retains the strength and kind set at its start. 3. The summary says there are four upgrade opportunities and one offers an alternative, so you cannot upgrade all five cards.
answers.evidence: Upgrading Action cards: stays in slot, next action capability, immediate condition status, four ways and cannot upgrade all cards.

answers.answer: 1. Cards I draw/discard counts at strengths 1–5 are: 1 draw/discard 1; 2 draw/discard 1/0; 3 2/1; 4 2/0; 5 3/1. 2. A required discard may be either a newly drawn card or one already in your hand.
answers.evidence: Cards draw table and note that discard may be newly drawn or previously held.

answers.answer: 1. The seven categories are bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear and Petting Zoo animal. Bears count as a category even when also herbivore or predator; Petting Zoo animal is its own category. Both count unless explicitly excluded.
answers.evidence: Animal categories (7); shared principles includes bear and Petting Zoo animal unless explicitly excluded.

answers.answer: 1. Association II permits exactly one donation, only if you performed at least one Association task in the same action; it needs no worker. 2. Pay the smallest currently visible donation amount, place one player token from your supply on that space, and gain 1 conservation. The printed ladder is 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10, then 12. Skip spaces blocked at setup. 3. Once all except the final space are covered, each later donation costs 12 and places no additional token.
answers.evidence: Association II donation rule and printed donation costs, token and repeatable last-space procedure.

answers.answer: 1. Zoo icons comprise the upper-right icons on Animal and Sponsor cards, partner-zoo and university icons, and water/rock requirement icons at upper left. Left-side conditions and Conservation Project icons are not zoo icons. 2. An effect can count its own card's icons; double icons count twice and trigger matching effects twice. 3. Card text takes priority over general rules.
answers.evidence: Association icon-count project and shared principles: counted icon locations, self-counting, doubled icons, card text priority.

answers.answer: 1. A requirement for two water/rock spaces means two distinct adjacent terrain hexes; if several edges touch one hex, it counts only once, and a larger terrain region contributes only the hexes actually adjacent. 2. Connected terrain regions do not change this adjacency count. Decorative water/rock illustrations on tiles are not terrain spaces and do not count.
answers.evidence: Animal action terrain rule and shared principles: count distinct adjacent hexes; tile illustrations provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements.

answers.answer: 1. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants the player who puts it into play 1 reputation; merely supporting an existing one does not grant that reputation. 2. Breeding Program projects use the same condition for all three reward levels, so choose any currently available level that meets the condition and ordinary support rules.
answers.evidence: Release project rule: new card gives 1 reputation, later support does not; Breeding Program all three spaces same requirement, choose any available.

answers.answer: 1. Read X:Y as condition on the left and reward on the right. A condition with no number, or marked “per,” pays once for each fulfillment. 2. A numbered threshold pays only once; if several numerical thresholds are listed, use the highest one met.
answers.evidence: Shared principles: X left condition/Y right reward, unnumbered/per once per fulfillment, numerical thresholds once at highest met.

answers.answer: 1. Connected means uncovered and sharing an edge with a covered space; isolated means no adjacent covered space. 2. A border space lacks a neighboring map hex on at least one of its six sides. 3. “Your zoo” includes your played cards, map and personal supply; “any zoo” includes those for every player.
answers.evidence: Shared principles definitions of connected, isolated, border space, your zoo and any zoo.

answers.answer: 1. A unique building must be placed when its Sponsor is played; if it cannot be legally placed, the Sponsor cannot be played. No size-based construction payment is due. 2. Use its matching tile, colored face up, rotate freely but do not flip it; ordinary placement rules and printed terrain adjacency apply. 3. Unique buildings are not enclosures, cannot house additional animals and do not count as water or rock spaces.
answers.evidence: Unique buildings: mandatory placement, tile orientation, ordinary/terrain rules, no size payment, not enclosures/terrain.

answers.answer: 1. Finish the Animals action, including moving its Action card to slot 1, before performing an animal-granted action. Use the granted Action card normally and move it to slot 1 after that action. 2. A named Action cannot be replaced by the X-token alternative; Determination (Any Action) may choose the X-token alternative.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Action/Determination timing and card movement, named Action vs Any Action X-token choice.

answers.answer: 1. Assertion/Dominance search the unused face-down base-project deck: take the selected project (Assertion) or named project (Dominance) into hand, then return the deck. 2. Dominance has no effect if its named project is already in play. 3. Later play the obtained card through Association conservation work above the board and support it immediately; it does not go into the setup base row below the board.
answers.evidence: Assertion/Dominance clarification: unused base deck, no effect if already in play, later card placed above board through Association.

answers.answer: 1. Boost and Clever resolve after finishing Animals and moving the Animals card. 2. Clever puts its chosen Action card in slot 1; cards formerly left of it shift right. Boost puts its named card in slot 1 or 5; moving to slot 5 shifts cards formerly to its right left.
answers.evidence: Boost/Clever clarification: after Animals movement; slot choices and shifts.

answers.answer: 1. A target zoo must have at least 5 appeal for Constriction, Hypnosis, Pilfering and Venom. 2. The playing animal's appeal may be gained before or after its interactive effect; ordinarily its new appeal need not be counted in selecting targets. 3. If the multiplayer group prefers, it may use the cards' alternate text marked for solo instead; this does not require playing solo mode.
answers.evidence: Interactive abilities eligibility and target reference; ability appeal may be ordered before/after; multiplayer alternative text.

answers.answer: 1. Constriction affects every other eligible zoo ahead of yours on appeal and/or conservation. Place tokens on its highest slots: one token on slot 5 if ahead on one track, or tokens on slots 4 and 5 if ahead on both. 2. Do not stack two Constriction tokens on one card; return duplicates. 3. Each affected action loses 2 strength, for each execution of a multiplied action; X-tokens can restore strength. 4. Return a token after acting with that card; otherwise it is removed without effect at the break.
answers.evidence: Constriction target reference and detailed token placement, no stacking, -2 strength, multiplied actions and expiry.

answers.answer: 1. A card reduced to effective strength zero or below may not be used as a regular action unless you spend enough X-tokens to bring it to at least 1. 2. Alternatively, use its alternative X-token action, or leave it until it is at least in slot 3.
answers.evidence: Constriction: at effective strength zero or below, boost to at least one, use alternative X-token action, or wait until slot 3 or higher.

answers.answer: 1. Yes. With Digging, decide again after each card and may choose either option each time: discard a display card and replenish it, or discard a hand card and draw one deck card. You may choose either option up to twice. 2. A display card discarded through Digging is replaced immediately, shifting higher folders down and drawing into folder 6.
answers.evidence: Digging 2 clarification: choose up to twice and decide again after each; display discard replaced immediately.

answers.answer: 1. A flock animal may avoid taking a new enclosure only if another herbivore in your zoo requires at least the flock animal's standard-enclosure size. 2. The same qualifying herbivore can host any number of flock animals and need not be a flock animal. 3. A later non-flock herbivore cannot join the flock animal in its enclosure. 4. When releasing a flock animal, follow the usual occupied-enclosure freeing/fallback procedure; you do not need to establish historical accommodation, since exact past residents are not tracked.
answers.evidence: Flock Animal clarification: eligible host, unlimited use, later non-flock cannot share, release procedure and no historical tracking.

answers.answer: 1. Full-throated activates the lowest remaining reserve worker by moving it to your notepad for immediate use. 2. Take a last-worker map reward if shown. 3. If all workers are already active, the ability has no effect.
answers.evidence: Full-throated clarification: lowest reserve worker, map reward, no effect if all active.

answers.answer: 1. Hunter reveals the specified number of deck cards, adds one revealed Animal card to hand and discards the others. If none revealed is an Animal, discard all revealed cards and add none.
answers.evidence: Hunter X clarification: reveal X, add one Animal, discard all others; if no Animal, discard all.

answers.answer: 1. Choose among tied players for highest appeal; if you yourself are the target, Hypnosis has no effect. 2. Copy only a card in target slot 1, 2 or 3, using that owner's upgraded/unupgraded side; your own X-tokens may be spent. 3. Move the borrowed card to slot 1 normally. Venom and Constriction tokens on it apply to you and are discarded afterward; its Multiplier cannot be used.
answers.evidence: Hypnosis detail: ties/self, slots 1–3, target's card side, own X-tokens, card movement and tokens.

answers.answer: 1. Place a gained Multiplier immediately on its named Action card; a bonus-tile Multiplier may go on any card, including Animals. 2. On its next use, execute the action twice consecutively at the same base strength and move the card only after both executions. Each X-token boosts only one execution. 3. Defer after-finishing effects until both executions are done. A break triggered by the first execution waits until the whole turn finishes. 4. Return used tokens to supply; an unused token is removed at the next break.
answers.evidence: Multiplier clarification: placement, two executions, X-token assignment, effect/break timing, token return/expiry.

answers.answer: 1. Two Multiplier tokens permit up to three executions, not four. 2. A multiplied X-token alternative may take two X-tokens, subject to the five-token holding limit, but you may not mix one X-token action with one regular action.
answers.evidence: Multiplier: each additional token adds one execution; multiplied X-token alternative and no mixing.

answers.answer: 1. Peacocking lets you place the Large Bird Aviary before upgrading Build. 2. You must not already have an Aviary and must have a legal site; other placement restrictions remain, including Build II for upgrade-marked spaces. 3. Posturing follows normal placement rules, including kiosk spacing, and multiple buildings are placed one at a time.
answers.evidence: Peacocking/Posturing clarifications: Aviary exception and limits; ordinary restrictions and sequential placement.

answers.answer: 1. Successive Petting Zoo animals grant 3, then 6, then 9 appeal. 2. One Petting Zoo can hold at most three. 3. Petting Zoo animals count as small animals.
answers.evidence: Petting Zoo animal: first 3, second 6, third 9 appeal; one enclosure holds three; they count as small.

answers.answer: 1. Pilfering 1 selects the highest-appeal eligible zoo; Pilfering 2 separately selects highest appeal and most conservation, resolving the targets separately. Ties let you choose. 2. The most-conservation target must have at least 1 conservation. 3. A self-target has no effect.
answers.evidence: Interactive target reference and Pilfering X: ties, conservation leader needs at least one, self-target no effect.

answers.answer: 1. The target chooses whether to give 5 money or permit a random hand-card draw; Final Scoring cards cannot be drawn. 2. If target has no hand cards, they must give 5 money; if they have less than 5 money, they must give a card. With neither a card nor 5 money, they give all current money, including zero. 3. Resolve repeated Pilfering sequentially, and the target may choose differently each time.
answers.evidence: Pilfering X details payment choice, random hand card, exceptions for lack of money/cards, and repeated resolution.

answers.answer: 1. Pouch lets you tuck up to X hand cards beneath the animal for 2 appeal per card; tucked cards have no remaining function. If that animal is released, discard its tucked cards too, while keeping the appeal already gained. 2. Sunbathing sells up to X hand cards for 4 money each and puts sold cards in the discard pile.
answers.evidence: Pouch X and Sunbathing X clarifications.

answers.answer: 1. If Resistance drew an extra Final Scoring card before the 10-conservation discard milestone, it joins the cards you can choose from when discarding one at that milestone. 2. At game end, score every remaining Final Scoring card; each card has its own maximum of 4 conservation points.
answers.evidence: Resistance clarification: extra card joins milestone choice; every remaining card scored with individual four-point cap.

answers.answer: 1. Scavenging shuffles the discard pile face down, draws randomly from it, makes the card's stated selection, then returns the discard pile face up. For Scavenging 3, draw 3 random cards, keep 1 and discard the others.
answers.evidence: Scavenging clarification: random face-down draw and Scavenging 3 example.

answers.answer: 1. Snapping takes exactly one card from the display regardless of reputation; it does not offer a deck draw instead. 2. Sponsor Magnet takes display Sponsor cards regardless of reputation range; if no Sponsor is present, it does nothing. Ordinary end-of-turn display refill applies.
answers.evidence: Snapping and Sponsor Magnet clarification; ordinary display refill.

answers.answer: 1. Venom X places X tokens on the affected player's cards in the lowest slots first (slot 1, then 2, etc.), at most one per card; duplicates return to supply. 2. Using a marked card removes its token and avoids all Venom fees that turn, including by using the alternative X-token action if you hold fewer than 5 X-tokens. 3. At turn end, pay 2 money only if you removed no Venom token that turn and at least one Venom token remains. If unable to pay, undo the turn and choose another action; spending all money cannot avoid the fee. Unused tokens expire without effect at the next break.
answers.evidence: Venom X clarification: placement/no stacking, use and fee condition, inability to pay, break expiry.

answers.answer: 1. Veterinarian immediately gives 2/5/10 money for having 1/2/3 universities. 2. It changes Conservation Project work to require Association strength 4 instead of 5. 3. Its final reward is 1 conservation for three universities.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 203 Veterinarian.

answers.answer: 1. Medical Breakthrough counts projects previously supported using the number of player tokens missing from your zoo map's left edge; its instant reward is 2 appeal per such project. 2. At each break it gives 1 conservation.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 206 Medical Breakthrough.

answers.answer: 1. Basic Research grants 1 conservation per pair of different continent/animal-category icons. 2. For every conservation point you gain from it, each other player gains 2 money.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 207 Basic Research.

answers.answer: 1. Science Library gives 1 appeal per research icon when played. 2. Whenever any player plays a research icon, the Science Library owner gains 2 money. 3. It scores 1 conservation if its owner has five different animal categories.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 208 Science Library.

answers.answer: 1. Expert on the Americas gives 1 appeal per Americas icon at play. 2. Each Americas icon played permits a free kiosk, under normal placement and spacing rules. 3. Its final condition is five or more kiosks, for 1 conservation.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 210 Expert on the Americas.

answers.answer: 1. Expert on Australia gives 1 appeal per Australia icon when played. 2. For each Australia icon played, you may tuck one hand card under it for 2 appeal; tucked cards have no further function.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 212 Expert on Australia.

answers.answer: 1. Each of Global Breeding Program and Breeding Program puts two supply tokens on the Sponsor. When supporting a base project below the Association board, return exactly one token as one icon; never use both for one support. 2. A base-origin card later played above the board does not qualify. 3. Their final condition scores 1 conservation for five or more project supports, counting missing left-map tokens.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 215/218 Breeding Programs.

answers.answer: 1. Engineer lets each Build action add one extra copy of a building built in that same action, without additional strength; pay its normal money and obey placement rules. Even with several different buildings, only one extra building is allowed. 2. You cannot exceed the one-per-zoo limit for each special enclosure type. 3. Final reward: 5 appeal with a full map except water/rock.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 217 Engineer.

answers.answer: 1. Diversity Researcher gives 2 money per water/rock icon immediately. 2. You may build over water/rock spaces and ignore terrain requirements for animals and unique buildings, although their printed terrain icons still count. 3. Covered terrain no longer counts for Hydrologist, Geologist or Architectural Zoo; terrain need not be covered to qualify for a full map. 4. It scores 2 appeal per water-icon/rock-icon pair, up to three pairs.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 219 Diversity Researcher.

answers.answer: 1. Archaeologist triggers when an actual placement bonus on a border space is gained. 2. It lets you choose any uncovered placement bonus on your map as an additional bonus; it need not be on the border. Multiple triggers allow multiple extra choices, which may repeat the same bonus; resolve in chosen order. 3. Final reward: 1 conservation when all building border spaces are covered, excluding water/rock.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 221 Archaeologist.

answers.answer: 1. Migration Recording gives 1 X-token immediately. 2. Each Release into the Wild support gains 1 additional conservation. You may support the same release project repeatedly with different qualifying animals, but at most once per project per Association action. 3. Each token counts as a separate project support for other effects.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 224 Migration Recording.

answers.answer: 1. Quarantine Lab gives 1 X-token immediately. 2. It makes you immune to Venom, Constriction, Hypnosis and Pilfering. For Hypnosis and Pilfering, ignore your counters and find the next qualifying player. 3. It scores 1 conservation if you have all five continents.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 225 Quarantine Lab.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Special Assignment lets you permanently choose small or large, mark that choice with a supply token, and reveal deck cards until finding an Animal of that type; keep it and discard the rest. 2. You can no longer play the opposite size type. 3. Chosen small animals get +2 appeal, chosen large animals +4; size-3 animals remain legal but get no bonus.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 227 WAZA Special Assignment.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Small Animals Program gives 2 money per small animal immediately. 2. An Animals action containing only small animals qualifies: you may play one additional small Animal from hand with normal costs/rules, then take one small Animal from the display into hand regardless of reputation. 3. You may take the display card even if you declined the extra play; mixing a large animal into the original action disqualifies it.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 228 WAZA Small Animals Program.

answers.answer: 1. Hydrologist gives 1 appeal per water icon on play. 2. Each newly covered space adjacent to water gives 1 money, including multiple spaces within one building; one space adjacent to multiple water hexes still pays only once. 3. It scores 1 conservation if all water hexes are connected (none isolated).
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 241 Hydrologist.

answers.answer: 1. Barred Owl Hut places its unique building. Whenever a bird icon is played, draw two cards from the deck, keep one and discard the other.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 249 Barred Owl Hut.

answers.answer: 1. Sea Turtle Tank places its unique building adjacent to water. 2. Each reptile icon played lets you sell up to two hand cards for 4 money each; discard the sold cards.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 250 Sea Turtle Tank.

answers.answer: 1. Spotted Hyena Compound triggers Hunter for each predator icon played, with cards revealed equal to your total predator icons. 2. A card with two predator icons triggers two sequential Hunters, counting both new icons for each Hunter's draw amount.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 252 Spotted Hyena Compound.

answers.answer: 1. Okapi Stable places its unique building and three supply tokens on the Sponsor. 2. Per herbivore icon played, you may spend one token to play a Sponsor from hand for money equal to its level, following normal conditions. The Stable's own herbivore icon can trigger this when it is played; there are three uses total.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 253 Okapi Stable.

answers.answer: 1. Zoo School gives 1 reputation and 1 conservation. 2. Place its unique building so that it covers at least two border spaces. 3. Then take one in-range display card or draw one deck card; resolve simultaneous benefits in the order you choose.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 254 Zoo School.

answers.answer: 1. Side Entrance may be placed on two border spaces without touching an existing building; other placement rules apply, and later buildings may attach to it. 2. At each break it yields 2 money per adjacent building except empty standard enclosures; it may be adjacent to a kiosk. 3. Its final reward is 5 appeal with full map coverage excluding water/rock.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 257 Side Entrance.

answers.answer: 1. Native Farm Animals gives 1 appeal per connected uncovered building border space; water and rock do not count. 2. At game end it grants 1 conservation per six contiguous empty building spaces, evaluating each group separately (example: groups of 13, 6, 3, 2 yield 3 conservation total). 3. Restricted/upgrade-marked building spaces count even without Build II; terrain spaces are excluded.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 260 Native Farm Animals.

answers.answer: 1. Explorer gives 2 money per different continent or animal-category icon; research icons do not count. 2. Each continent/category newly introduced to your zoo gives 1 appeal and 2 money. A newly played card with two copies of the same new icon grants this novelty benefit only once.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 262 Explorer.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Large Animal Program may place a free size-5 standard enclosure under normal placement rules. 2. When playing a large animal, it lets you ignore one left-side condition, such as a required icon or Animals upgrade; terrain requirements cannot be ignored. 3. It stacks with Research Institute, allowing two conditions to be ignored.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 263 WAZA Large Animal Program.

answers.answer: 1. Biodiverse Zoo compares each animal category in your zoo with the player to your right, and gives 1 conservation for each category in which you have more icons. 2. If that player has none of a category, one of your icons is enough to exceed them. 3. Maximum is 4 conservation.
answers.evidence: Base Final Scoring and map clarifications: Biodiverse Zoo 009.

answers.answer: 1. Observation Tower's bonus applies only to standard enclosures adjacent to the tower hex itself, not merely another rock hex. 2. Special enclosures do not qualify. 3. Housing an animal there grants the two appeal again even if an earlier animal was released. 4. The tower is not a building for kiosk income.
answers.evidence: Map 1 Observation Tower clarification.

answers.answer: 1. Outdoor Areas qualifies standard enclosures touching the Outdoor Area hex itself, not merely another water hex. 2. Such an enclosure counts as two spaces larger for all purposes after placement, and the bonus cannot be ignored for release or transfer. 3. It does not affect special enclosures and is not a building.
answers.evidence: Map 2 Outdoor Areas clarification.

answers.answer: 1. Commercial Harbor activates when a building is placed on its adjacent building space. Your first building may start beside the Harbor but need not. 2. Its discard ability may be used before, during or after your action, once per own turn only; never during breaks or another player's turn. 3. The Harbor is not a building.
answers.evidence: Map 4 Commercial Harbor clarification.

answers.answer: 1. Park Restaurant income is 1 money per adjacent covered hex, not per building. Empty enclosures count, regardless of occupancy or building type. 2. The Restaurant is not a building and does not count as a kiosk neighbor building. 3. Its special-enclosure bonus grants either one free Reptile House or one free Large Bird Aviary, even before Build II; choose one, not both, and obey other normal placement rules.
answers.evidence: Map 5 Park Restaurant clarification.

answers.answer: 1. Cover each H space by placing a building under ordinary placement rules; when covered, reveal cards until a Sponsor appears, keep it and discard the others. 2. H spaces are not placement bonuses, so do not trigger Archaeologist. 3. After all three are covered, every Sponsor's level is one lower. 4. Bonus partner zoos still require Association II for the third/fourth partner, and bonus buildings still require Build II for upgrade-marked spaces.
answers.evidence: Map 8 Hollywood Hills clarification.

answers.answer: 1. Pay money equal to the Sponsor's level and meet its usual conditions. 2. This bonus lets you play the card only from hand, even with Sponsors II. 3. It does not move the Sponsors Action card from its current slot.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ: paid Sponsor bonus cost/conditions, hand-only source, no Sponsors card movement.

answers.answer: 1. Appeal cannot exceed 113 and conservation cannot exceed 41; any gains beyond those track ends are lost. Reputation has a separate overflow rule.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ: appeal 113 and conservation 41 caps; excess gains lost.

answers.answer: 1. Venom targets every other zoo with higher appeal than yours and at least 5 appeal. 2. Hypnosis targets the highest-appeal eligible zoo, with the actor choosing ties; self-target has no effect, and only slots 1–3 may be copied. 3. Pilfering 1 targets the highest-appeal eligible zoo; Pilfering 2 separately targets highest appeal and most conservation (the latter must have at least 1 conservation); actor chooses ties and self-targets do nothing. 4. Constriction affects every other eligible zoo ahead of yours on appeal and/or conservation; one token if ahead on one track and two if ahead on both.
answers.evidence: Interactive target reference and detailed Hypnosis/Pilfering/Constriction descriptions.

answers.answer: 1. An Animal card's partner-zoo condition requires a partner zoo from that Animal's continent; a Sponsor's partner-zoo condition permits a partner zoo from any continent. 2. A red maximum-25 appeal condition permits play only while you have at most 25 appeal; it is not a general appeal cap. 3. A minimum-reputation condition requires at least its printed value. 4. An ignore-one-condition bonus removes one left-edge requirement, but not a terrain requirement.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ: partner condition distinctions, maximum 25, minimum reputation, and ignore-one-condition bonus.

answers.answer: 1. Crested Porcupine's Digging 2 provides up to two selections, choosing each time between discarding a display card and immediately replenishing it, or discarding a hand card then drawing a deck card. 2. The two choices may differ; decide again after each card.
answers.evidence: Digging 2 clarification: its two options and choose up to twice/again after each.

answers.answer: 1. After taking display cards, move higher-folder cards down into gaps while preserving their order, then fill empty spaces from the deck. 2. At a break, discard folders 1 and 2 first, move the remaining cards down, then refill. The summary does not state a separate alternate ordering for final empty folders beyond filling them from the deck.
answers.evidence: Reputation track/display: move cards from higher folders down keeping order, then fill empties from deck; break display procedure.

answers.answer: 1. Build a standard enclosure empty side up, showing its yellow border and size number. 2. Gain each placement bonus covered immediately once, resolving all covered bonuses before the next building; occupying the enclosure later does not award those bonuses again.
answers.evidence: Build action: new standard enclosure empty side up; each placement bonus immediately once, with no second reward on later occupancy.

answers.answer: 1. When the first player reaches or passes 10 conservation, all players choose and discard one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining Final Scoring pile.
answers.evidence: Conservation track: at 10, all players choose/discard one Final Scoring card face down under remaining pile.

answers.answer: 1. Randomly determine the starting player; ordinary turns proceed clockwise. 2. The game has no formal rounds: players take turns one at a time until the end is triggered. 3. A regular turn consists of one action using one of the five Action cards; resolve any extra effects/bonuses as specified by that action and card text.
answers.evidence: Setup: randomly determine start player, clockwise; Overview: no formal rounds; Turn Structure: one action on your turn.
